question: Which Switzerland-based institution releases the annual World Competitiveness Index?
solution:
The correct answer is __**IMD Business School**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IMD Business School**, located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, releases the **annual World Competitiveness Index**.
 
• The **World Competitiveness Index** evaluates the ability of countries to foster an environment where enterprises can achieve sustainable growth, generate jobs, and increase the overall welfare of their citizens.
 
• IMD’s World Competitiveness Center publishes this report annually, analyzing **64 economies** globally based on their competitiveness.
 
• The index is based on a combination of **hard data** (e.g., GDP, trade statistics) and **survey data** from business executives, covering categories like **economic performance**, **government efficiency**, **business efficiency**, and **infrastructure**.
 
• This index is widely regarded as a vital tool for governments, businesses, and other stakeholders to understand and improve their competitive standing in the global economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IMD Business School:**

 
 
• The **International Institute for Management Development (IMD)** is an independent academic institution that specializes in executive education and leadership development.
 
• IMD is located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, and is recognized globally for its expertise in the field of management and its impactful research reports like the **World Competitiveness Index**.
 
• It was founded in **1990** following the merger of two business schools from Nestlé and Alcan, and is consistently ranked among the top business schools globally.
 
 
 
• **World Competitiveness Index:**
 
 
• This index has been published annually since **1989** by the IMD World Competitiveness Center.
 
• It evaluates **64 economies** worldwide based on four broad pillars: **economic performance**, **government efficiency**, **business efficiency**, and **infrastructure**.
 
• It considers over **330 criteria**, including quantitative and qualitative indicators, to assess the competitiveness of a nation.
 
 
 
• **Competitiveness in the Global Economy:**
 
 
• Competitiveness refers to the ability of a country to create and maintain an environment in which enterprises can sustainably compete, grow, and improve the living standards of its citizens.
 
• Factors like innovation, infrastructure, education, governance, and economic stability play a critical role in determining competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Other Institutions and Indices:**
 
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):** Publishes the **Global Competitiveness Report**, which is separate from the IMD's index but also evaluates global competitiveness.
 
• **University of Geneva:** Primarily focuses on research and education in various academic disciplines, but it does not publish any competitiveness index.
 
• **ETH Zurich:** Known for its expertise in technology and engineering, ETH Zurich is a leading academic institution in Switzerland but is not associated with the World Competitiveness Index.
 
• **University of St. Gallen:** This Swiss university is renowned for its research in management, economics, and law, but it does not release the World Competitiveness Index.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **World Competitiveness Index** is one of the most comprehensive studies on the global competitiveness of nations, providing valuable insights for policymakers and business leaders.
 
• While several institutions publish reports on competitiveness, the IMD’s index is unique due to its heavy reliance on survey data from business executives, offering a practical perspective on economic realities.
 
• The report helps stakeholders identify strengths and weaknesses, fostering reforms to improve economic performance and quality of life.
 
• Countries like **Switzerland**, **Singapore**, and **Denmark** often rank highly in this index, reflecting their strong economic foundations and governance systems.
